newsitem.title: USA: Footwear shares bound higher, many on busy volume.
newsitem.headline: Footwear shares bound higher, many on busy volume.

text.p: Shares in a host of shoe companies jumped on Wednesday as an industry report showed improving pricing trends for the sneaker market.

The report, based on a survey of 30,000 consumers and issued by the Athletic Footwear Association, said spending on athletic footwear rose to $3.66 billion for the first four months of the year versus $3.36 billion in 1995.
The report also showed the average price of a pair of sneakers for the four months was $34.09 compared to $32.53 for all of 1995 and $31.19 in 1994.
However, reasons for the rally extended beyond the survey.
Reebok International Ltd, for example, announced it would buy back 17 million shares for $36 per share under a Dutch auction self-tender, and shares rose 5/16 to 35-7/8.

Nike, which rose 1-1/8 to 119-1/2, "has been on a tremendous run," said Dean Witter analyst Scott Emerman. "Their business trends are very positive and the same thing is true for Fila (Holdings SpA) ".
Also, analysts said it was unclear whether the survey had triggered the widespread buying that sent even recent laggard Stride Rite Corp surging 1-1/8 to 8-3/4 on volume of nearly 1.7 million shares.

"It's possible, but it's really odd to see Stride Rite and Finish Line Inc up like this on the same day," said Gruntal analyst Susan Silverstein. "There really is some excessive volume out there on Stride Rite.
Spokesmen at Stride Rite, which makes the Keds line of sneakers and Finish Line, a specialty retailer of authletic footwear and leisure wear, were not available for comment.
Finish Line Inc shares rose 2-1/2 to 31.
